'''Lev Aleksandrovich Shuvalov''' ({{langx|ru|Шувалов Лев Александрович}}; 15{{nbsp}}November 1923 – 6{{nbsp}}December 2004) was a Soviet crystallographer and mathematician. Shuvalov is notable for his work on symmetry considerations in [[Ferroelectricity|ferroelectric]] crystal phase changes.

==Career==

Shuvalov was born on 15 November 1923. In 1941 he entered the army directly from school. Shuvalov participated in the battles of [[Battle of Moscow|Moscow]], [[Battle of Stalingrad|Stalingrad]] and [[Battle of Kursk|Kursk]]. He served until the end of the war in 1945 and was awarded the [[Order of the Red Star]].<ref name=obituary1>{{cite journal |title=Lev Aleksandrovich Shuvalov (November 15, 1923–December 6, 2004) |journal=Crystallography Reports |date=May 2005 |volume=50 |issue=3 |pages=528–529 |doi=10.1134/1.1927621 |bibcode=2005CryRp..50..528. }}</ref><ref name=Blinic>{{cite journal |last1=Blinc |first1=Robert |title=In memoriam Lev Aleksandrovich Shuvalov 1923-2004 |journal=IEEE Transactions on Ultrasonics, Ferroelectrics and Frequency Control |date=January 2005 |volume=52 |issue=1 |page=9 |doi=10.1109/TUFFC.2005.1397344 |bibcode=2005ITUFF..52....9B }}</ref>

In 1946 Shuvalov entered [[Moscow State University]] to study physics, graduating in 1951. He then worked for the [[Hydroproject]] Institute for five years. In 1956 Shuvalov joined the [[Shubnikov Institute of Crystallography RAS| Institute of Crystallography]] studying under [[Alexei Vasilievich Shubnikov]]; he gained his doctorate in 1971. He was then appointed a professor at the Institute of Crystallography. In 1972 Shuvalov created the Laboratory of Phase Transitions of which he was the head for over 20 years.<ref name=RAS>{{cite web |title=ШУВАЛОВ Лев Александрович Шувалов Л.А.(1923–2004) |trans-title=SHUVALOV Lev Alexandrovich Shuvalov L.A.(1923-2004) |url=https://www.crys.ras.ru/1221-ob-institute/istoriya-instituta/istoriya-v-litsakh/shuvalov-l-a/1199-shuvalov-l-a |publisher=Institute of Crystallography of the USSR Academy of Sciences |access-date=9 August 2025 |language=Russian}}</ref>

Shuvalov's work was in the fields of mathematics and crystallography, specifically the use of [[group theory]] to analyse the [[Phase transition|phase changes]] occurring in [[Ferroelectricity|ferroelectric]] and [[Ferroelasticity|ferroelastic]] crystals. He published more than 700 papers during his scientific career and held over 20 patents.<ref name=RAS/>

Between 1956 and 1974, Shuvalov was a leader in the field of symmetry considerations in the crystallography and crystal physics of ferroelectrics. Shuvalov investigated symmetry changes during ferroelectric, ferroelastic and ferromagnetic phase transitions based on [[Curie's principle]].<ref name=obituary1/><ref name=Blinic/> He established a classification of ferroelectrics based on their crystal symmetry.<ref name=RAS/> In the 1980s and 1990s Shuvalov led a team that researched new families of ferroelectrics and [[Antiferroelectricity|antiferroelectrics]] such as the alkali trihydrosulfates and trihydroselenites.<ref name=Blinic/><ref name=Taylor>{{cite journal |last1=Taylor |first1=George W. |title=Obituary: Lev A. Shuvalov (1923-2004) |journal=[[Ferroelectrics (journal)|Ferroelectrics]] |date=August 2005 |volume=322 |issue=1 |pages=1–2 |doi=10.1080/00150190500321168 |bibcode=2005Fer...322....1T }}</ref> He also discovered a new class of crystals with superionic conductivity (superprotonic conductors).<ref name=RAS/>

Shuvalov was editor of ''[[Kristallografija]]'' from 1997 to 2004.<ref>{{cite journal |title=On the 50th Anniversary of the journal Kristallografiya (Crystallography Reports) |journal=Crystallography Reports |date=January 2006 |volume=51 |issue=1 |page=1 |doi=10.1134/S1063774506010019 |bibcode=2006CryRp..51....1. }}</ref> He also served on the editorial boards of international journals such as ''Condensed Matter News'', ''[[Crystallography Reviews]]'', ''[[Ferroelectrics (journal)|Ferroelectrics]]'', ''Ferroelectrics Letters'', and ''[[Zeitschrift für Kristallographie – Crystalline Materials|Zeitschrift für Kristallographie]]''.<ref name=Taylor/>

A special issue of ''Ferroelectrics'' was dedicated to Shuvalov in 1989.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lemanov |first1=V. V. |last2=Janovec |first2=V. |title=Professor Lev Aleksandrovich Shuvalov—a tribute |journal=Ferroelectrics |date=October 1989 |volume=98 |issue=1 |pages=xv–xvi |doi=10.1080/00150198908217562 |bibcode=1989Fer....98D..15L }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kobayashi |first1=Jinzo |title=Lev Aleksandrovich Shuvalov—my bosom friend |journal=Ferroelectrics |date=October 1989 |volume=98 |issue=1 |pages=xvii |doi=10.1080/00150198908217563 |bibcode=1989Fer....98D..17K }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Blinc |first1=Robert |title=Tribute to professor Lev A. Shuvalov |journal=Ferroelectrics |date=October 1989 |volume=98 |issue=1 |pages=xix |doi=10.1080/00150198908217565 |bibcode=1989Fer....98D..19B }}</ref> Shuvalov died on 6 December 2004 in [[Moscow]].

A symposium in honour of the centenary of Shuvalov's birth was held at [[MIREA – Russian Technological University]] in 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=Topical issues in the physics of ferroelectrics and related materials |url=https://english.mirea.ru/news/a-symposium-with-international-participation-topical-issues-in-the-physics-of-ferroelectrics-and-rel/ |publisher=MIREA - Russian Technological University |access-date=9 August 2025}}</ref>

==Publications==

Selected publications available in English:

* 1956: Ferroelectric phase transitions and crystal symmetry<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zheludev |first1=I. S. |last2=Shuvalov |first2=L. A. |title=Ferroelectric phase transitions and crystal symmetry |journal=Soviet Physics Crystallography |date=1956 |volume=1 |issue=6 |pages=537–542 |url=https://archive.org/details/crystallography-reports_november-december-1956_1_6/page/536/mode/2up |access-date=10 August 2025}}</ref>
* 1960: Ferromagnetic phase transitions and the symmetry of crystals<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Shuvalov |first1=L. A. |title=Ferromagnetic phase transitions and the symmetry of crystals |journal=Soviet Physics Crystallography |date=1960 |volume=4 |issue=3 |pages=371–380}}</ref>
* 1963: [[Dichromatic symmetry|Antisymmetry]] and its concrete modifications<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Shuvalov |first1=L. A. |title=Antisymmetry and its concrete modifications |journal=Soviet Physics Crystallography |date=1963 |volume=7 |issue=4 |pages=418–422}}</ref>
* 1963: Limit groups of [[Multiple antisymmetry|double antisymmetry]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Shuvalov |first1=L. A. |title=Limit groups of double antisymmetry |journal=Soviet Physics Crystallography |date=1963 |volume=7 |issue=6 |pages=669–672}}</ref>
* 1964: Crystallographic classification of ferroelectrics, ferroelectric phase transformations and peculiarities of domain structure, and some physical properties of ferroelectrics of the different classes<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Shuvalov |first1=L. A. |title=Crystallographic classification of ferroelectrics, ferroelectric phase transformations and peculiarities of domain structure, and some physical properties of ferroelectrics of the different classes |journal=Soviet Physics Crystallography |date=1964 |volume=8 |issue=4 |pages=495–500}}</ref>
* 1970: Symmetry aspects of ferroelectricity<ref>{{cite conference |last1=Shuvalov |first1=L. A. |title=Symmetry aspects of ferroelectricity |conference=Proceedings of the 2nd International Meeting on Ferroelectricity [Kyoto, 1969]|journal=Journal of the Physical Society of Japan |date=1970 |volume=28 (supplement) |pages=38–51}}</ref>
* 1988: Modern Crystallography IV: Physical properties of crystals<ref>{{cite book |editor-last1=Shuvalov |editor-first1=L. A. |title=Modern Crystallography IV: Physical Properties of Crystals |date=1988 |publisher=Springer Berlin / Heidelberg |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |isbn=9783642818387}}</ref>
* List of publications from the [[Steklov Mathematical Institute]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Shuvalov, Lev Aleksandrovich (1923–2004): List of publications |url=https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/person101058 |website=Math-Net.ru |publisher=Steklov Mathematical Institute RAS |access-date=9 August 2025}}</ref>

==Awards==

* [[Order of the Red Star]]
* [[USSR State Prize|State Prize of the USSR]] in the field of science (1975): "For a series of works on the crystallography and crystal chemistry of ferroelectrics." See: [[:ru:Лауреаты Государственной премии СССР в области науки и техники (1967—1975)|ru:Laureates of the State Prize of the USSR in the field of science and technology (1967—1975)]]
* [[Named prizes and medals of the Russian Academy of Sciences#Physical sciences|Federov Prize]] (1994): "For a series of works on the theory of symmetry, phase transitions, piezoelectric and related materials." See: [[:ru:Премия_имени_Е._С._Фёдорова|ru:E. S. Federov award]]
